nodes.title: Video+Audio Reference
widgets_values: If your video has an audio channel you need, right now you must manually drag the audio output from Load Video node to the ref_video_audio_0 input on the top left of the workflow. Currently, the Load Video node creates a critical error when trying to export audio from a video that has none, so I cannot programmically account for that with a toggle in this workflow!

nodes.title: Temporal Upsampling (De-Roping)
widgets_values:
This option detects areas of quick motion in your gen and duplicates the frames allowing the model to regenerate them correctly, removing the duplicated frames at the end. The result effectively cleans smudgy, blurry, lossy artifacts caused by distance and high velocity. It is recommended for any shots that aren't stationary dialogue scenes!

The amount of deroping steps is set to 1/2 of your main stage steps.

nodes.title: Custom Forced Audio
widgets_values: Custom Audio: if enabled, <Audio 1> will completely replace the gen's audio latent, forcing video to match what it hears -- great for lipsyncing dialogue shots in either T2V/I2V, or REF2VA! Just make sure the audio duration is close to the video gen duration, and that any dialogue is written clearly in <d>dialogue</d> tags in the prompt (improves lipsync).

Ref2va Template Example for Char Ref Sheet + BG + Voice Ref
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the character in <Picture 1>. (describe character attributes if needed)
<Subject 2> is the location in <Picture 2>. (describe location details)
<Audio 1> is the voice-timbre reference for <Subject 1>. (audio 1 should be 15 sec of a person talking)

summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] A cinematic scene located in <Subject 2> of <Subject 1> speaking.

retention_analysis:
<Audio 1>: reference - its vocal timbre guides the vocal delivery of <Subject 1> without copying the original signal.

detailed_description:
[Shot 1]: <Subject 1> is standing in front of the camera in <Subject 2> while staring out into the distance. She speaks the line of dialogue in <Audio 1>: <d>What's next, strap a leash on me? I'm not a pet cat, you weirdo!</d>. She has a flippant and sarcastic expression as she speaks. 
[Shot 2] at 00:05: A profile view medium shot of <Subject 1> as she turns towards the camera and walks off the frame.

overall_soundscape:
(Describe ambience, specific sounds to address)

non_diegetic_music:
N/A

Prompting Guide
widgets_values:
https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/docs/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_ref_en.md

ref2va is EXTREMELY programmatic. Meaning, the instructions you give must be accurate for consistent results. Use the above guide to reference the instructional keywords/tags for use in your own prompts. You can be creative and use natural language for most situations.

Does it have to be as complicated? Not really. But according to the prompting guide, the model likes firm instructions like this.
